web.markdown:
We estimate Google is the largest single owner of AI compute, holding about one quarter of global cumulative capacity as of Q4 2025. Notably among hyperscalers, Google’s compute comes primarily from its own custom TPU chips rather than NVIDIA’s GPUs.

Google is likely the largest owner of AI compute, driven by custom TPUs

![Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/assets/logo/epoch-full-standard.svg)\|CC-BYepoch.aiDownload graph

Note that Microsoft and Meta also have in-house-designed chips that we do not currently track, though we believe these have a negligible impact on our estimates.

Epoch's work is free to use, distribute, and reproduce provided the source and authors are credited under the Creative Commons BY

## Learn more about this graph

Using estimates from the [AI Chip Owners hub](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-owners), we show the cumulative amount of AI compute held by each of the world’s four largest compute owners: Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon, as of Q4 2025. We break out compute by chip manufacturer and find that Google held the most compute as of Q4 2025, driven by its in-house-designed TPU chips.

### Data

The [AI Chip Owners hub](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-owners) tracks how much computing capacity is held by different entities, broken down by specific chip models, beginning in Q1 2022. These figures include Nvidia and AMD datacenter GPUs, Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium and Inferentia chips, and Huawei’s AI chips. We estimate that these five categories encompass the [vast majority](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-sales-documentation#other-ai-chips) of the world’s dedicated AI computing power. Meta and Microsoft also have their own custom AI chip programs, which are not included here, but they produce far fewer chips than Google’s and Amazon’s. For more details on the methodology used to estimate ownership, see our [AI Chip Owners documentation](https://epoch.ai/data-insights/data/ai-chip-owners-documentation#overview).

### Limitations

We convert chip computing capabilities into H100 equivalents (H100e) based on their relative FLOP/s specifications, specifically their maximum 8-bit specification. However, different chips have different strengths and weaknesses (e.g., memory capacities and bandwidths, software stability).Depending on the use case, an H100e provided by an MI300X chip may be more or less effective than an H100e provided by a TPUv6 or B300 chip. Conversions are thus approximate, and are most accurate for model training, which is typically compute rather than bandwidth-bottlenecked.

Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle collectively hold an estimated 71% of the world’s cumulative AI compute as of Q4 2025, measured in H100-equivalents of computing power. This is up from 63% in Q1 2024.

Many AI labs (including OpenAI and Anthropic) largely depend on these hyperscalers for access to R&D and inference compute.

Epoch's work is free to use, distribute, and reproduce provided the source and authors are credited under the Creative Commons BY
license.

## Learn more about this graph

We calculate the aggregate amount of compute (in H100-equivalents) held by Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle, as a share of the global total each quarter. These five largest hyperscalers own a combined 71% of compute as of Q4 2025, rising from 63% in Q1 2024.

### Data

Chip ownership data comes from Epoch AI’s AI Chip Owners dataset, which tracks chip acquisitions by major entities from Q1 2022 through Q4 2025. The dataset covers chips manufactured by Nvidia, Google, AMD, Huawei, and Amazon. We focus on the period 2024 through 2025 because Google’s TPUs are only tracked from 2023 onward and using less than one year of past data results in unstable aggregate figures.

### Assumptions and limitations

Our Chip Ownership data does not capture all global chip ownership, and has weaker coverage prior to 2023. Q1 2026 data is excluded as it was not yet finalized at time of analysis.

The H100-equivalent unit uses a chip’s highest 8-bit operation/second specifications to convert between chips. The actual utility of a particular chip depend on workload assumptions, so H100e does not perfectly reflect real-world performance differences across chip types.

# Google Possesses 23% of Global AI Computing Capacity via TPU Chips

Google's TPU chips power Gemini AI model, reducing costs versus NVIDIA-dependent rivals

[By Park Ji-min](https://www.chosun.com/english/people/park-jimin/)

Published 2026.04.08. 15:12Updated 2026.04.08. 16:35

A survey has revealed that Google possesses AI chips equivalent to a quarter of the global AI computing (processing) capacity. As the AI competition shifts toward computational power beyond model performance, analysis suggests that Google's strategic advantage is becoming evident, as it possesses both its own chip, the Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), and the AI model Gemini.

![Graphics by Kwon Hye-in](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/VME3DHGE65AJDHCXQD736Y2SUI.png?auth=bd9dd9396ee86cbda45c721f949f3793a4879e1cc9df3f4a0888d734c1dd30f8&width=480&height=748&smart=true)

Graphics by Kwon Hye-in

U.S. non-profit research institute Epoch AI unveiled the "AI Chip Holder Explorer," which tracks the AI semiconductor holdings of major companies, on the 6th, local time. They compiled corporate earnings reports and industry estimates to track how AI chips are distributed. The number of AI chips held by each company was aggregated by converting them based on the performance of NVIDIA's older-generation AI chip, the 'H100'. For example, since the 7th-generation TPU can perform 2.3 times the computation of the H100, if a company has 1 million of these, it is calculated as having 2.3 million H100s.

As of the fourth quarter of last year, global companies were found to hold 21.3 million AI chips based on the H100 standard. Among these, Google possessed the most with 5 million chips, accounting for 23% of the total. Hyperscalers—companies operating large-scale data centers—such as Microsoft (3.4 million), Amazon (2.5 million), and Meta (2.3 million) followed.

Of the 5 million AI chips held by Google, 3.8 million were found to be its own TPU chips. This contrasts with other companies, whose AI chips are mostly NVIDIA products. Google uses TPUs for the training and inference of its AI model Gemini. While AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic rely on borrowing AI chips from hyperscalers, Google is reducing costs and enhancing AI performance through its own chips. Industry experts view Google as the only company to have internalized the entire AI ecosystem, spanning semiconductors, cloud, and models.

Meanwhile, Chinese companies held only 1.1 million AI chips, accounting for just 5% of the global total. This is less than the holdings of a single major tech company. Approximately 64% of China's AI chips were Huawei's Ascend chips. This is attributed to U.S. export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China.
